#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reviewer's K2 check: the applied list as the launch script's own parser reads it; every non-comment line parsed;
each brief line's kind against its brief's front matter; every hash among the owner's recorded approvals.

    python3 k2_check.py <launch script> <list file> <tree> <APPROVED.before>
"""
import hashlib
import importlib.util
import os
import re
import sys

script, listfile, tree, before = sys.argv[1:5]
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("indep_launch_review_k2", script)
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(m)
data = open(listfile, "rb").read()
b0 = open(before, "rb").read()
print("head is APPROVED.before byte for byte:", data[:len(b0)] == b0, f"({len(b0)} of {len(data)} bytes)")
t, b = m.parse_approved(data)
print("parse_approved: template lines", len(t), "brief lines", len(b))
lines = data.decode("utf-8").splitlines()
comments = [x for x in lines if x.lstrip().startswith("#")]
noncomment = [x for x in lines if x.strip() and not x.lstrip().startswith("#")]
parsed = [x for x in noncomment if re.fullmatch(r"([0-9a-f]{64})\s+(template|brief)\s+(.+?)\s*", x)]
print(f"lines {len(lines)}: comments {len(comments)}, non-comment {len(noncomment)}, of which parsed {len(parsed)}")
OWNER = {
    "bbff1249953bd9d3b2596b33a108712bdddd79a7e86723b9e6955e3d6b0e9068": "labeller v3 (DEC-1113; DIF 400-404; DECL §12)",
    "e13b5f96d0e058277f3ec3014f13205d7fe0bc950cfc308e81b3ee3d742ac904": "labeller-2 v3 (DEC-1113; DIF 400-404; DECL §12)",
    "82134b3dd6b5a077abfc2eb6fa7481f0f5a73eab60396cfbd655042d53027c57": "writer-tuning v3 (DEC-1113; DIF 400-404; DECL §12)",
    "137a73d1df4c265fd5ce4e24716797703e2b12dcaeb90663c0170834a60fafe6": "writer-heldout v3 (DEC-1113; DIF 400-404; DECL §12)",
    "b212a424062e402b0a25ee4a157ae14a0af798d0ad973aa33dacd730782be6ab": "overlap-auditor v1 (DIF 400-404; DECL §12)",
    "51c459cfbcfec47652df455844480a56a5bc91b5fba3bcf57dc807c5dbf08cc2": "operator brief.md (DEC-1109 (1); ACT-OPERATOR-1)",
    "e86703304144f7d0c3f48332478f696d8f704c540f5ecf6c0551f6bd761ff81a": "operator reviewer-brief.md (DEC-1109 (1))",
}
for p, hs in sorted(t.items()):
    have = hashlib.sha256(open(os.path.join(tree, p), "rb").read()).hexdigest()
    print(f"  template {p}: {'ok' if hs == {have} else 'MISMATCH'}")
for h, k, p in b:
    blob = open(os.path.join(tree, p), "rb").read()
    fm = m.front_matter(blob)
    fk = fm.get("kind") if fm else None
    print(f"  brief {k:9} {p}: bytes {'ok' if hashlib.sha256(blob).hexdigest() == h else 'MISMATCH'}; "
          f"owner-approved: {OWNER.get(h, 'NO')}; front-matter kind {fk!r}; "
          f"kind matches front matter {fk == k}; a launch kind {k in m.KINDS}")
print("duplicate brief lines:", len(b) - len(set(b)))
print("brief lines whose hash is not an owner approval:", sum(1 for h, _, _ in b if h not in OWNER))

say() { printf '\n== %s (%s)\n' "$*" "$(date -u +%H:%M:%S)"; }
bad() { echo "REVIEW FAIL: $*"; FAILS=$((FAILS + 1)); }
ok() { echo "ok: $*"; }
AP() { ( cd "$R" && bash "$D/apply.sh" "$@" --sets-root "$PR" ); }
expect() { grep -Eq "$2" "$1" && ok "$3" || bad "$3 (wanted /$2/)"; }
snap() { ( cd "$PR" && find . -printf '%M %s %p\n' 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort ); }
launch() {  # kind brief sha set commit [extra]

  ( cd "$R" && HOME=$PH python3 "$R/$SCRIPT" --sets-root "$PR" --kind "$k" --brief "$b" --brief-sha256 "$s" \
      --commit "$c" --set "$set" "$@" --seed 17 --dry > "$W/launch.out" 2> "$W/launch.err" ); local rc=$?

cmp -s "$L" "$REF/drafts/APPROVED.before" && ok "the list byte for byte APPROVED.before ($(sha256sum "$L" | cut -c1-12)), mode $(stat -c %a "$L")" || bad "the list is not as before"
echo "governance/project/: $(ls -A "$R/governance/project" | tr '\n' ' ')"
echo "drafts: $(ls -d "$D"/backup* | sed "s#$D/##" | tr '\n' ' ')"

git -C "$R" diff --cached --name-status
git -C "$R" commit -q -m "ACT-W2-149-INSTALL-1 undone (review rehearsal)" --trailer "Task: DAEO-sdxk" \
  --trailer "Implements: DEC-1101, DEC-1112" --trailer "Role: owner" || bad "the undo commit"
git -C "$R" show --stat --format='%h %s' HEAD
AP check > "$W/c3.txt" 2>&1; echo "check exit $?"; tail -1 "$W/c3.txt"
expect "$W/c3.txt" "ready to apply" "ready to apply again"
snap > "$W/sets-2.txt"; diff "$W/sets-0.txt" "$W/sets-2.txt" && ok "the planted root as at the start (names, modes, sizes)" || bad "the planted root differs after the undo"

say "negative cases"
AP undo > "$W/n1.txt" 2>&1; echo "undo in the before state: exit $?"; tail -1 "$W/n1.txt"
chmod u+w "$L"; printf '# a later line\n' >> "$L"; chmod 0400 "$L"
AP check > "$W/n2.txt" 2>&1; echo "check, the list neither before nor applied: exit $?"; tail -2 "$W/n2.txt"
AP apply > "$W/n3.txt" 2>&1; echo "apply, the same: exit $?"; tail -1 "$W/n3.txt"
chmod u+w "$L"; cat "$D/APPROVED.before" > "$L"; chmod 0400 "$L"
AP apply > "$W/n4.txt" 2>&1; echo "apply again: exit $?"; tail -1 "$W/n4.txt"
chmod u+w "$D/backup/APPROVED"; printf 'x\n' >> "$D/backup/APPROVED"
AP undo > "$W/n5.txt" 2>&1; echo "undo with a damaged backup: exit $?"; tail -1 "$W/n5.txt"
cat "$D/APPROVED.before" > "$D/backup/APPROVED"
AP undo > "$W/n6.txt" 2>&1; echo "undo with the backup mended: exit $?"; tail -1 "$W/n6.txt"
cmp -s "$L" "$REF/drafts/APPROVED.before" && ok "the list byte for byte as before after the second undo" || bad "the list after the second undo"

say "end"
du -sh "$W" | sed "s#$W#<w>#"
du -s --inodes "$W" | sed "s#$W#<w>#"
date -u '+end %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'
echo "failures: $FAILS"
SHEOF

## Findings

**F1 (K1) — the apply writes a bytecode cache into the tree.** `parse_check` loads the launch script under `python3 -I`, which still writes `governance/project/orchestration/tools/__pycache__/indep_launch.cpython-312.pyc`. My rehearsal showed it, and the main tree has none today, so the live apply would create it. It is not in the stated touched set. It is gitignored, so the commit is unaffected. Fix: `python3 -I -B`.
- Ordinary work: yes, because every apply (and every check in the applied state) writes it.
- Consequence: other.
- Scope: in.

**F2 (K1) — the §5 commit takes everything staged.** `git commit -m … --trailer …` has no path limit, so it commits everything staged in the shared main tree. The only guard is the operator reading `git diff --cached` ("expect exactly 5 A"), and the message does not say to stop if more is listed. Fix: `-- governance/project/indep-briefs/sgx1`. Also note the undo's harmless warning.
- Ordinary work: yes, because the main tree is shared by the CTO's sessions.
- Consequence: other. Another session's staged change would be committed under this ACT's message; nothing is lost.
- Scope: in.

**F3 (K5) — the order check can refuse falsely.** `$SETS_GLOBS` is unquoted (`drafts/apply.sh:65`), so bash expands the four globs against the caller's folder. From a folder holding `runs/x/misses.jsonl`, `check` said "ACT-SETS-GLOBS-1 is not applied"; from a folder without one, it was ready.
- Ordinary work: no, because the main tree's root has no `runs/` folder and no tracked match.
- Consequence: other (fails closed).
- Scope: in.

**F4 (K5) — a later script change forces a rebuild.** `LAUNCH_SHA` pins the launch script exactly, and `APPROVED.after`'s comment names that hash and the merge commit. If any change to `indep_launch.py` merges first (the wiring follow-up must change it), `check` and `apply` refuse with "merge it first". `freeze.py` would then change `APPROVED.after`, `apply.sh` and the package sha, which means a new review and a new yes. So §3's "this ACT stands" holds only if the ACT is applied first, and the package does not say so.
- Ordinary work: yes, because the follow-up is the next planned step.
- Consequence: other (fails closed).
- Scope: in.

**F5 (K6) — the package states the wrong class and reason.** It says class (b), and that no rule names these paths. In fact the `walled-sessions` row names both as (O), and the higher vote applies, so the class is O.
- Ordinary work: yes, because the digest would carry the wrong class and reason.
- Consequence: other (the routing is the same).
- Scope: in.

**F6 (K7) — the declared pin cannot serve these briefs.** The launch script reads the brief at `--commit` (`indep_launch.py:1332`), the same commit it builds the tree from (LAUNCH-SPEC §1). The declaration pins every wall's tree at `f000adda4`, where no brief exists. A launch there was refused 10 with `brief_sha256` null and `template_ok` true. The declaration must be re-pinned at or after this ACT's commit. Its own §2 already requires a new pin, because the live hook and map changed with ACT-SETS-GLOBS-1 (`97a84e770058`/`40085090306e` became `74f8dbea4761`/`44f99ea563cb`).
- Ordinary work: yes, because the CTO would launch at the declared pin.
- Consequence: other (fails closed).
- Scope: in.

**F7 (K8) — the exclusion should be an entry criterion, not a recommendation.** Residual 2 says "recommended", but DEC-803 makes this feature-gated risk an entry criterion of the follow-up. The change is `governance/project/indep-briefs/**` in `tree-exclude.txt`, an owner-approved template change, landing at or before the new pin. Without it, an ordinary tree-wide Grep for a decision id surfaces the other labeller's brief. The auditor's copies of the labellers' briefs show that script labels carry no `reason`, which could hint which of x and y is labeller 1.
- Ordinary work: yes, once set-up A runs.
- Consequence: other for this ACT, because nothing can run until the follow-up lands.
- Scope: in.
